title: Impacts of floating-point non-associativity on reproducibility for HPC and deep learning applications
problem: Floating-point non-associativity causes run-to-run variability in parallel programs, accumulating errors in iterative algorithms and deep learning pipelines. This non-reproducibility prevents effective correctness testing, certification, and bug detection.
motivation: Non-reproducibility critically affects the efficiency of correctness testing, robustness assessment, and commercial certification, especially as deep learning and HPC become increasingly integrated.
method: Investigated how floating-point non-associativity—where adding numbers in different orders produces slightly different results because computers round intermediate calculations differently—affects parallel programs through direct measurement. Tested the performance and productivity impact of replacing atomic operations (synchronized actions between processors) with deterministic alternatives on GPUs. Examined PyTorch's built-in reproducibility features to assess how reliably they work. Evaluated whether specialized hardware like the Groq LPU accelerator can automatically enforce reproducible deep learning inference without requiring algorithmic or software changes.
key_novelty: A specialized hardware accelerator (Groq LPU) can automatically enforce reproducible results in deep learning inference without requiring algorithmic or software modifications.
contributions: Statistical investigation of floating-point non-associativity in parallel programming models
Analysis and quantification of performance trade-offs when replacing atomic operations with deterministic alternatives on GPUs
Evaluation of PyTorch's deterministic options with assessment of documentation reliability and completeness
Validation that hardware-based determinism improves reproducibility and correctness for deep learning inference

metrics.other: performance and productivity overhead of deterministic alternatives
